intent_en: To demonstrate the dramatic increase in the number of students taking the SAT from 1941 to the present day.
previous_intent: To illustrate the dramatic surge in the number of students taking the SAT over the decades, highlighting the link between growing test participation and intensifying college competition.
narration_support: In 1941, just 10,000 students took the SAT. By 1950, 80,000 students took the exam. By 1960, 800,000 students took the SAT. By the next decade, it rose to a million. And now, more than 2 million students take the exam.
chart_support: Bar chart showing the number of students taking the SAT increasing from 1941 to the present, with bars growing significantly taller over time.
evidence_note: The narration details the specific growth in student numbers over decades, while the bar chart visually confirms this upward trend from 1941 to 'Now'.
